title: Fed’s hawkish rate hold keeps pressure on Bitcoin: Analysts
summary: Traders are pricing in a 78% chance of a December rate hike, while analysts say Treasury yields, the US dollar and upcoming inflation data could determine Bitcoin’s next move.
content: The Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates while maintaining a hawkish stance has increased pressure on Bitcoin. Traders are pricing in a significant chance of a December rate hike. According to analysts, upcoming inflation data, Treasury yields, and the movement of the US dollar will likely dictate Bitcoin's next major price direction in the near term.

content_ta: குளோபல் செக்யூரிட்டீஸ் ஃபைனான்ஸ் துறையில் செயல்திறனை மேம்படுத்தவும், கணக்கீட்டு பிழைகளைக் குறைக்கவும் வடிவமைக்கப்பட்ட விநியோகிக்கப்பட்ட முறையான DLT பிளாட்ஃபார்மான Equilend-ன் 1Source பிளாட்ஃபார்மில் Goldman Sachs இணைந்துள்ளது. பிற முன்னணி நிதி நிறுவனங்களுடன் இணைந்து இந்த DLT பிளாட்ஃபார்மின் ஒரு பகுதியாக மாறுவதன் மூலம், செயல்பாட்டு மேம்பாடுகளையும் செலவுக் மிச்சத்தையும் கொண்டுவர Goldman Sachs உதவும்.

title: iPipeline Introduces Next-Generation Professional Services Model to Drive Technology Adoption ROI
summary:
iPipeline®, a leading global provider of comprehensive and integrated digital solutions for the life insurance and financial services industry, today announces the launch of iPipeline Services CORE Methodology and its Client Value Group to bring customers a new consultative paradigm for professional services, defined by faster time-to-value, transparent timelines and costs, tailored solutions that meet specific business needs, and ongoing optimization through continuous support models. Together, the initiatives transform iPipeline’s professional services model to help customers implement technology more efficiently, increase adoption, and realize measurable business value faster.
iPipeline Services CORE Methodology addresses an important industry need for professional services to simplify complex technology transformations and deliver continuous value through a consultative approach built around four guiding principles: Client, Outcomes, Rapid, and Execution. The framework starts with understanding each client’s business goals and definition of success, measures performance by business impact rather than activity, accelerates delivery through standardized models, AI-enabled processes and proven best practices, and brings disciplined, consultative execution to every engagement. Instead of focusing solely on one-time implementations, iPipeline’s advisors will deliver ongoing AI-augmented optimization and highly transparent, personalized client engagement. AI-enabled delivery models that accelerate timelines and improve consistency underpin an outcome-driven approach to help agents, carriers, financial institutions, and wealth managers realize return-on-investment faster.
The expanded Professional Services offering includes Consulting, Implementation Packages, Quality-as-a-Service (QaaS), Managed Services, and Training-as-a-Service (TaaS), creating a connected set of services designed to support clients throughout the professional services lifecycle. iPipeline’s new QaaS capabilities use automated testing to improve quality and reduce deployment timelines, while TaaS  provides flexible, on-demand education that enables clients to scale adoption across their organizations.
Mike James, EVP, Professional Services at iPipeline, commented on the new offering, “The landscape of technological innovation is changing as more insurers modernize their operations with operational and AI solutions. Our long-standing relationships with life insurance and annuities providers at every point of the financial and insurance ecosystem give us a ground-level view into their most pressing needs as they work to help everyday people with financial planning and security. Through our CORE Methodology and Client Value Group, we are responding to a growing need for more consultative services tailored to each company’s unique business requirements.”
iPipeline’s new Client Value Group complements the CORE Methodology team in elevating the traditional service provider role into that of a collaborative partner, helping clients identify where value exists within their business and determine how best to unlock it. As an expansion of iPipeline’s business development department, the Client Value Group will provide expert advisory services that align technology and workflows and apply targeted services to improve speed, efficiency, and growth outcomes.
Through a structured Value Levers framework, the Client Value Group will help clients identify and prioritize opportunities for impact, connect relevant implementation, consulting and optimization services, and provide continuous guidance as their business needs change. While CORE defines how iPipeline delivers services, the Client Value Group provides the expert guidance and insight needed to help clients make confident decisions and maintain progress over time.
Together, iPipeline’s Services CORE Methodology team and Client Value Group will act as clients’ digital transformation advocates, providing guidance on where to drive impact and measuring success through business impact and outcomes rather than project completion. Predictable pricing and scalable offerings, including packaged and managed services, give users  greater control and confidence while helping improve delivery predictability and reduce implementation risk. Through end-to-end implementation, advisory, and optimization services, iPipeline will help clients achieve better business outcomes, including accelerated time-to-value, greater adoption, operational efficiency, continuous improvement, and ROI from their life insurance and annuities solutions.
“The decision to adopt and integrate new insurance technology can be a complex, high-stakes endeavor,” said Pat O’Donnell, Chief Executive Officer at iPipeline. “As operational, AI, and data solutions become more sophisticated, it is no longer enough for a solution provider to install, instruct, and go home. This evolution brings together seasoned solution providers who understand the industry, proven delivery models, and advanced technology to ensure solutions are implemented efficiently, adopted effectively, and are continuously improved over time.”
The announcement comes on the heels of iPipeline’s recent integration of iGO Evolve®, iPipeline’s AI-optimized life insurance e-application solution, as the first module on the new Novera AI-First Digital Platform for Life, Annuities and Wealth Powered by CHARLi™, the AI foundation connecting the iPipeline ecosystem. The platform underscores iPipeline’s broader commitment to combining advanced technology with consultative services that accelerate adoption and maximize long-term client value.

title: Former Swift CEO joins stablecoin firm OpenTrade as chairman
summary: Lazaro Campos takes the board role as the London-based company reports $300 million in assets locked and more than $1 billion in annual transaction volume.
content: Lazaro Campos, the former CEO of Swift, has joined London-based stablecoin firm OpenTrade as its new chairman. The appointment comes as the company reports significant milestones, including $300 million in assets locked and over $1 billion in annual transaction volume, highlighting its growing presence in the digital asset and financial technology sector.

title: Solana wallet Solflare pledges to pay missed rewards on staked $160 million after validator goes offline
summary: About 1.56 million SOL sat on a validator that stopped earning, and the wallet still hasn’t named the firm that held its keys.
content: Solana wallet Solflare has pledged to cover missed rewards for users after a validator went offline, affecting approximately 1.56 million staked SOL valued at around $160 million. The validator stopped earning rewards due to the outage. However, the wallet provider has not yet publicly disclosed the specific firm responsible for holding the keys to the affected validator.
content_ta: Solana வாலெட் ஆன Solflare, ஒரு வேலிடேட்டர் ஆஃப்லைனில் சென்றதைத் தொடர்ந்து, பயனர்களுக்கு விடுபட்ட ரிவார்டுகளை வழங்குவதாக உறுதியளித்துள்ளது. இதனால் சுமார் $160 மில்லியன் மதிப்புள்ள 1.56 மில்லியன் staked SOL பாதிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. இந்த செயலிழப்பு காரணமாக வேலிடேட்டர் ரிவார்டுகள் ஈட்டுவதை நிறுத்தியது. இருப்பினும், பாதிக்கப்பட்ட வேலிடேட்டரின் கீகளை வைத்திருந்த குறிப்பிட்ட நிறுவனத்தை வாலெட் நிறுவனம் இன்னும்公开 வெளியிடவில்லை.

title: Coast Raises $35 Million to Build the Financial Platform for the Physical Economy
summary:
Coast, the financial platform built for the physical economy, today announced it has raised $35 million in new growth equity funding. The round was led by Thomvest Ventures and joined by new investors Intuit Ventures, Small World Capital, and Alpha Square Group, with participation from existing investors ICONIQ Growth, Accel, Insight Partners, Better Tomorrow Ventures, Avid Ventures, Vintage Investment Partners, Colle Capital, Synchrony, RXR, and The Fintech Fund.
The funding will expand Coast into a broader financial operating system for the physical economy. Coast will use the proceeds to reach more customers and to invest in AI-powered expense automation, new Bill Pay and Accounts Payable products, and embedded partnerships with the fleet and field service platforms its customers already use.
The AI data center boom is pulling construction, HVAC, electrical, utility, and transportation into overdrive. Job postings for HVAC engineers have risen nearly 78% since 2022, and openings for electricians, welders, and construction specialists are up 30%. As these industries grow, their businesses are getting more complex. But the tools they rely on haven't evolved. Most are still forced to piece together generic corporate cards, banking, and fleet tools that weren't designed for how they operate.
Coast is the financial platform built for the physical economy: construction, HVAC, plumbing, landscaping, electrical, pest control, solar, transportation, energy, oil and gas, utilities, and more. The company started with America's top-rated fuel card, then expanded into corporate cards, expense management, and bill pay, all designed for how these businesses actually operate.
"The millions of field businesses that keep the physical economy running still lack a financial platform built around the way they work," said Daniel Simon, Founder and CEO of Coast. "Coast is that platform. We're excited to deepen our partnership with Thomvest, who first backed Coast in 2024, and to welcome Intuit Ventures, a deep integration partner that's a critical part of so many of our customers' businesses as they grow."
Coast's industry focus gives customers controls and data that go far beyond a typical corporate card: vehicle- and driver-level visibility, telematics-enabled controls, fuel grade and gallon-level detail, job costing, and payments for trade-specific workflows and fuel, field, supplies, and office needs. That depth extends to accounting, with integrations that automate reconciliation and coding for finance teams. Taken together, the Coast platform saves a customer tens of thousands of dollars and weeks of work that could instead be spent growing their business.
"The physical economy has been underserved by financial software for decades, and Coast is changing that with a platform that brings payments and credit controls into the workflows that businesses already use," said Don Butler, Managing Director at Thomvest Ventures. "We believe that software that acts as a control plane for payments and credit, embedded in the workflows of vertical industries, is one of the most important shifts happening in financial services. Coast is a clear leader on both fronts."
Coast steers drivers to the fueling and purchase options that are most efficient for the company, with approvals and reconciliation running automatically through the systems each customer already relies on. New Bill Pay and Accounts Payable products bring vendor invoices onto the same platform as card spend, giving customers one view of all outgoing money and marking the first step toward a full financial services suite for physical economy businesses. Through partnerships with telematics, fleet management, and field service providers like Samsara and Fleetio, operators can use vehicle location, driver identity, and odometer data to catch an off-route fuel purchase or shut off a card without leaving the software they use to run the fleet.

title: Hyphenate Raises $45M Series A Following 86x Revenue Growth as CFOs Move to Autonomous Finance
summary:
The first wave of finance AI helped teams work faster. The next is taking responsibility for the work itself. Hyphenate, the autonomous finance platform for the office of the CFO, today announced a $45 million Series A led by Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from B Capital and existing investors including Foundation Capital, BoldCap and Gaia Ventures.
Inside Hyphenate customers, agents are already reconciling cash, processing sales orders, running invoicing, maintaining subledgers and moving the close forward, with finance teams stepping in only where judgment changes the outcome. The round, which brings total funding to $54 million, comes less than a month after Maximor rebranded to Hyphenate, as customers expand its use across the office of the CFO. The company will use the capital to take its agents deeper across the finance function and into strategic finance.
“Every finance team carries a long list of work it does because somebody has to,” said Ramnandan Krishnamurthy, co-founder and CEO of Hyphenate. “Our customers are watching that list shrink in production. Once a team sees the system handle one workflow to an auditor’s standard, they hand it the next one. That is the pattern this company is built around, and this round lets us run it across the whole function.”
12 months from seed to 86x
Hyphenate raised a $9 million seed one year ago to take repetitive work off finance teams. Since then, the company has passed multi-million-dollar ARR, its agents have taken on work across hundreds of entities, thousands of bank accounts and millions of transactions every day, and customers report 90% less repetitive finance work and 75% fewer audit exceptions. The more telling number is what customers do next: 40% expand within their first year, several by two to three times, and the average customer runs six modules.Companies are handing the system larger parts of finance once it has proved itself in one workflow.
What that looks like in production
The expansion is now visible in production, at companies where finance errors carry real cost.
Mini Melts USA, the consumer goods company, runs Hyphenate agents on top of its SAP environment for orders, invoicing and refunds. Within three months of going live, the company was getting back 16,640 hours of finance work a year.
HiBid, one of the largest online auction platforms in North America, has run more than $2.5 billion in GMV through full order-to-cash automation on Hyphenate. Invoicing, collections and cash application across that volume now run as a single continuous process, and the company has cut its month-end close from three weeks to one day.
Groupon, the Nasdaq-listed marketplace, is replacing legacy and home-grown systems with Hyphenate across treasury, order-to-cash and more than a dozen subledger processes.
“As a public company, we run finance at a scale where every number has to stand up to scrutiny: millions of transactions, multiple currencies and markets, and auditors who need the evidence behind all of it. We’re replacing legacy and home-grown tools with Hyphenate because it’s built for that bar, and we see it becoming the AI foundation for our entire finance organization,” said Rana Kashyap, CFO of Groupon.
Synthesia, the AI video platform, is rolling Hyphenate out across its finance function.
“As an AI company, we expect our own operations to run on AI. The breadth of the Hyphenate platform has improved every functional area of our accounting and finance operations. We replaced point solutions with an autonomous finance platform that understands our business. Now the team focuses on exceptions and analysis, which helps make decisions faster,” said Daniel Kim, CFO of Synthesia.
How Hyphenate works
Hyphenate sits on top of the ERP, banks and other systems a company already runs and connects them into a single shared finance context. The business keeps its systems of record and gains a layer that can act across all of it.
On that layer, agents work across five areas of finance: order-to-cash, treasury, GL accounting, procure-to-pay, and reporting and insights. In practice that covers revenue recognition, invoicing, collections, cash reconciliation, accruals, subledgers, AP, close and board reporting.
What sets the system apart is that it’s self learning. Instead of relying on forward-deployed engineers to build bespoke agents for each customer, Hyphenate trains on a company’s historical spreadsheets, emails and system logs, then replays past months to pick up the edge cases traditional software never handled: the tribal knowledge that has kept finance manual. From there, it gets better the longer it runs. An exception resolved during one close becomes precedent for the next. A policy decision made once is applied every time the same situation appears. Every action carries its evidence with it, so the output is audit-ready by default. Month by month, the share of routine work handled autonomously rises, and the finance leader’s involvement narrows to the decisions that require judgment.
The trust threshold is moving
Finance has been one of the hardest functions for AI to enter autonomously. Research commissioned by the company earlier this year found that 96% of CFOs saw freeing teams for strategic work as AI’s biggest benefit, while only 14% completely trusted AI to produce accurate accounting data independently. Ninety-seven percent said human oversight was critical.
Hyphenate’s growth suggests a path through that tension. Autonomy does not require giving an AI system unrestricted control. It requires giving it responsibility within clear boundaries, preserving evidence behind every action and involving a human at the moments where judgment changes the outcome.
“What makes Hyphenate compelling is that autonomy is already showing up in customer operations,” said Abhishek Sharma, Managing Director at Nexus Venture Partners. “Finance has an unusually high bar for accuracy, controls and auditability. Hyphenate has built around that bar from the beginning, and the expansion we are seeing inside customers shows what becomes possible once the system earns the right to take on more work.”

title: Airtm and BVNK Partner to Expand Wallet-Native Payments to Emerging Markets

The announcement, made today at the Stellar Meridian Conference, comes as Airtm launches Airtm Connect, which allows digital asset companies around the world, including BVNK, to build wallet connections with Airtm's global user base. Through the integration, Airtm users will be able to use funds held in their wallets to pay participating retailers enabled by BVNK, while also creating new ways to fund and receive money.
A Wallet-Native Approach to Global Commerce
The partnership unites two distinct capabilities: Airtm's deep roots in emerging markets and trusted position as a last-mile network, and BVNK's proven stablecoin payment infrastructure and on-ramp connectivity across global banking corridors.
And with BVNK now part of Mastercard, Airtm will also have access to the recently launched Mastercard Global Money Platform, a full-stack, modular infrastructure layer for fiat and stablecoin accounts, payments and money movement, while retaining the customer relationship and avoiding the complexity of integrating multiple providers.
The integration will leverage the Stellar blockchain, a high speed, low-cost payment rail which was recently added to the BVNK platform.
"We believe payments should move natively on-chain - it’s simply a better way to move money. But origination is only half the story. For stablecoin payments to truly work, origination and destination need to be tightly connected. That’s why we’re excited to partner with BVNK," said Rubén Galindo Steckel, CEO of Airtm. "BVNK has solved one of the hardest problems in fintech: reliable, compliant on-ramping at scale. At Airtm, we’ve spent the last decade building the destination layer for the global dollar economy. Together, we're closing the loop. The magic happens when users can fund it reliably and use it more easily in the real-world. That's what this partnership delivers. We're not just adding another integration. We're building the complete on-ramp-to-commerce flow that emerging market users have needed for years."
"We're excited to power Airtm's vision of wallet-native commerce," said Kimberly Mescal Julien, Global Head of Partnerships at BVNK. "Airtm Connect shows what's possible when fintech platforms stop thinking about wallets as silos and start treating them as distribution channels for real-world commerce. We're honored to be the infrastructure backbone."
Expanding Financial Infrastructure Options
BVNK's stablecoin payment capabilities add optionality to Airtm's existing financial infrastructure partners, allowing Airtm to serve customers across diverse funding paths and geographies. This flexibility is critical for a network that operates across multiple jurisdictions in the Global South, including markets where stablecoins are increasingly used as a payment and store of value option, and where regulatory certainty varies and liquidity corridors are fragmented.
"Our infrastructure strategy has always been about choice for Airtm and for our users," said Rubén Galindo Steckel, CEO of Airtm. "We're not betting on a single provider or payment rail. We're building a truly distributed last-mile network. BVNK strengthens that."

title: Noewe Accounting Raises Half a Million Euros to Transform the Traditional Accounting Services Model
summary:
The company was valued at €2.5 million in this investment round. The funding will support the development of an accounting service powered by artificial intelligence (AI) and automation, enabling small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to access structured financial data, CFO-level insights and tax recommendations on demand.
“I believe in the accounting model being developed by Noewe Accounting, where technology and professional expertise enable businesses to quickly obtain the financial and tax insights they need to make decisions. I see significant potential for this model in Lithuania and other European Union markets. I am committed to contributing to the project’s success not only through investment but also by actively participating in the development of technological solutions and commercial expansion. Together with the team, we aim to create a service that companies will regard as an essential tool for day-to-day business management,” says Philip Van Goethem, an investor based in Lithuania.
“We greatly appreciate Philip’s confidence in our team and the business we are building. An experienced investor’s decision to invest and actively contribute to the project is an important confirmation that we are on the right track and that the next-generation accounting services model we are developing has significant potential. Business leaders need to know what is happening in their businesses now. Information received a month later may explain past performance, but by then it is often too late to take action. That is why we are building Noewe Accounting to ensure clients receive structured financial data and the financial and tax insights derived from it in a timely manner, helping them make concrete business decisions,” says Gediminas Laucius, Managing Partner at Noewe
Technology Shortens the Journey from Transaction to Decision
The model being developed by Noewe Accounting addresses a familiar business problem: financial information often reaches decision-makers too late. At traditional accounting firms, where much of the work is performed manually, processing invoices and transactions, posting entries to the general ledger and preparing financial statements can take weeks. The data needed to make informed decisions may only become available a month later or even further down the line.
Automated data collection and processing, combined with AI solutions, will enable Noewe Accounting to significantly reduce the time between a business transaction taking place and its appearance in accounting records and management reports. Clients will no longer have to wait several weeks for large volumes of invoices and transactions to be processed. The funds raised will be allocated to developing technological solutions and refining the service model, laying the groundwork for further expansion in Lithuania and other EU markets.
Noewe Accounting will be responsible for selecting and implementing the technological solutions. Working together with each client, the company will assess how data flows through their operations, where work is being duplicated and which processes can be automated. This will improve the efficiency of the entire data-processing chain, on which the speed and quality of information depend.
CFO-Level and Analytical Expertise for Smaller Businesses
Faster data processing also transforms the nature of the accounting service itself. With less time spent on data entry and repetitive tasks, specialists will be able to analyse more deeply what drives a client’s profitability, where costs are rising, how cash flows are changing and what actions should be considered.
Small and medium-sized enterprises using Noewe Accounting’s services will be able to access high-level financial analysis, insights and advice that have traditionally been available mainly to larger companies with their own chief financial officers (CFOs) and financial analysis teams. Financial data will be complemented by assessments of the factors driving business performance, forecasts and specific recommendations for management.
“Clients need to understand why their margins are declining, when they might face a shortage of working capital or how a planned investment will affect their cash flow. Technology will enable us to prepare the data needed for analysis quickly, while our specialists will help assess the situation and possible courses of action. Clients will be able to access this expertise as needed, without having to establish a separate financial analysis department,” says Monika Šmigelskaitė, Head of Noewe Accounting.
Tax Monitoring and Advisory as Part of the Service
“Accounting data can reveal tax opportunities a company has yet to take advantage of, as well as areas where its operations present the greatest risks. Our goal is to turn this data into timely, actionable recommendations: which tax relief measures a company could use, which risks it should manage and how and how to optimise its tax position appropriately in light of its business activities and investment plans. These insights will become an ongoing part of the accounting service, helping business leaders make well-informed decisions,” says Sandra Pavlova, Partner at Noewe, heading the Corporate Tax Services practice.
The model draws on the accounting, tax, legal and strategic management expertise available across the Noewe Group. Automated financial analysis and tax assessments will help identify opportunities and risks in a timely manner and evaluate how potential decisions could affect profitability, cash flow and tax liabilities. When clients need to claim tax relief, implement recommended measures or take legal action, tax and legal specialists will provide support. This will enable clients to receive assistance throughout the entire process, from data-driven insights to the practical implementation of decisions.
“Small and medium-sized enterprises face complex financial and tax issues, yet maintaining an in-house team of specialists across all these fields is often too expensive. A technology-driven model allows us to make this expertise available as part of an everyday service. This is where we see the opportunity to fundamentally transform what businesses can expect from their accounting partner,” says G. Laucius.
